pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that seeded rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the '— high' and '— low' labels and that normal items have none.
test 'AC-3' checks high, low and normal filters with ids in order.
test 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all four views.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.

The behaviour is implemented in src/index.js and exercised by a test. But the last commit 'Follow-up edits' renamed that test from 'AC-7: …' to 'an unmatched filter names its priority…', so no test names AC-7 and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review'. An item no test names is unmet.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. test 'AC-8' checks it, and the traffic-config check now accepts the query.

findings.what: Commit 1431123 ('Follow-up edits') removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the title of the only test that covers AC-7. No test names AC-7 now. The change reads as a way to hide that the item is unnamed, and it contradicts the PR claim that the file covers AC-1 to AC-8.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7' in the test title, for example 'AC-7: an unmatched filter names its priority; an empty table says No items yet.'

findings.what: The body says test/priority.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8. That is no longer true after the rename, because AC-7 is not named in any test.
findings.fix: Restore the AC-7 test name, then the claim holds.

findings.what: The README documents the filter but not the '— high' and '— low' labels or the 400 on an invalid value.
findings.fix: Add one line on the labels and the 400.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's go and its decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled.
AC-7 is unmet because the last commit removed its name from the test. The other items are met, and every state-table row has a test.
The tests assert rendered output and status codes. I did not run them here; the project's CI covers that. The AC-7 naming problem is in the findings.
The README mentions the filter only.
The implementation is correct. It uses a parametrised query, validates against a Set, and escapes titles.
Input is validated against an allowlist and bound as a parameter. No injection found.
The diff adds only a minimal server-rendered nav and labels, with no UI framework or CSS files.
No browser flow or screenshots are provided; the page is plain server-rendered HTML.
The claim that the file covers AC-1 to AC-8 is false after the last commit. The other claims match the diff.
